from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework import permissions
from rest_framework.renderers import JSONRenderer
from rest_framework_csv.renderers import CSVRenderer
from .models import FinancialTransaction
from .serializers import TransactionSerializer

class TransactionExportView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]
    renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer, CSVRenderer]

    def get(self, request):
        # Content-negotiated scoping discrepancy
        if request.accepted_renderer.format == 'json':
            # Correctly scopes to current user's transactions
            queryset = FinancialTransaction.objects.filter(account__owner=request.user)
        else:
            # For CSV bulk exports, developer omitted user scoping!
            account_id = request.query_params.get('account_id')
            queryset = FinancialTransaction.objects.filter(account_id=account_id) if account_id else FinancialTransaction.objects.all()[:5000]

        serializer = TransactionSerializer(queryset, many=True)
        return Response(serializer.data)
diagnosis: TransactionExportView applies different queryset filtering based on the accepted renderer format. When responding with JSON, transactions are restricted to account__owner=request.user. However, when the caller requests CSV format (Accept: text/csv), the view fails to check account ownership, allowing any authenticated user to download arbitrary accounts' financial transactions or dump up to 5,000 transactions across all clients.

corrected_code:
from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework import permissions
from rest_framework.renderers import JSONRenderer
from rest_framework_csv.renderers import CSVRenderer
from .models import FinancialTransaction
from .serializers import TransactionSerializer

class TransactionExportView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]
    renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer, CSVRenderer]

    def get(self, request):
        # Uniformly enforce user ownership regardless of renderer format
        queryset = FinancialTransaction.objects.filter(account__owner=request.user)
        account_id = request.query_params.get('account_id')
        if account_id:
            queryset = queryset.filter(account_id=account_id)

        serializer = TransactionSerializer(queryset, many=True)
        return Response(serializer.data)
